artifacts.title: Dispatcher topology
artifacts.body:
Sequential pipeline: dispatch → reroute → scan
State entities: tech, dispatcher, parts, board

Each step advances a tech through its lifecycle in the logistics domain — the flow is the brief's own verbs, the state its own nouns (P0 lattice).

> Derivation: a single sequential flow over techs; no parallel, event, or failover topology is claimed beyond what the brief states.

artifacts.title: Data model & retrieval
artifacts.body:
Records: tech, dispatcher, parts, board
Operations: dispatch, reroute, scan

Each tech is the unit of state; dispatch steps read and write that state in order.

> Persistence is shaped by the brief's own nouns — no specific database or durable store is claimed beyond the brief.

artifacts.title: Integration surface (declared)
Security & authorization policy
artifacts.body:
Protected data: tech, dispatcher, parts, board (the brief's own entities).
Access model: tech, dispatcher — least privilege per role.

Authorization:
  • Each actor may act only on the techs its role owns.
  • Elevated actions outside an actor's scope are refused.
  • Sensitive tech data (identity, financial) is never logged in the clear.

> Policy above is a declaration derived from the brief's domain; the implemented isolation boundary is confirmed at the gate below (B-18 honesty).

artifacts.title: Validation + HITL contract
artifacts.body:
Validation contract (the HITL rules the engine actually enforces):
  1. Rejections require ≥12 characters of qualitative feedback (ADR-002).
  2. forceHuman gates (reframe, failed sandbox) can never be autopilot-approved.
  3. Phases execute strictly in order — the linear 0→12 graph.
  4. Every approval lands in the append-only decision journal.

Rejection policy: qualitative feedback is mandatory.
Diagnostics: one JSON event per orchestration step.

> - learning: IMPLEMENTED none | DECLARED self-learning-loop — P5 self-learning title only — no loop behind it (90 §10); write-back is M-08/G-25 roadmap.
